subject: Food Science
title: Temperature Abuse
description: A quick, practical guide to Temperature Abuse.

hook.text: The buffet sat out for four hours at room temperature. Next morning, 47 wedding guests were in the hospital.

buildup.text: Temperature abuse occurs when food stays in the danger zone—4°C to 60°C—long enough for bacteria to multiply.

discovery.text: The two-hour rule: discard perishable food left above 4°C for more than two hours. Above 32°C, the limit drops to one hour.

twist.text: Slow cookers can be dangerous on the 'warm' setting—if the temperature stays below 60°C, bacteria thrive instead of dying.

climax.text: Rapid cooling matters: hot food must drop from 60°C to 21°C in 2 hours, and to 4°C in 4 more hours—total of 6 hours.

punchline.text: Time in the danger zone is the enemy. Cold or hot—never in between.

quiz.question: What is the two-hour rule in food safety?
options: Cook food for two hours minimum
Discard perishable food left above 4°C for more than two hours
Refrigerate within two hours of purchasing
